November 11, 2026. You have 75 minutes. Steps 1 to 13 are 100 points. Step 14 is 10 points of extra credit.

Put your name in the subtitle at the top of this file. Follow the steps in order. Write the code for each step in the chunk under that step. Render to PDF. Submit this `.qmd` and the PDF before the 75 minutes are up.

The goal is a plot of mean potential against the standard deviation of sprint speed. The players in that plot have a simple name, a first name that starts with M, and a family name of at least 8 letters. A simple name has exactly two uppercase letters and exactly one space.

- You may use your notes and the R help files inside RStudio.
- You may use this course website, <https://amousavi1.github.io/612/data-612.html>, and David Gerard's data page for the database file, <https://dcgerard.github.io/stat_412_612/data.html>.
- You may not use Google, any other website, or an LLM.
- You may not communicate with anyone else.
- Use the tidyverse where a tidyverse verb exists. For text, use stringr. Step 14 is a function; base R is appropriate for the `stop()` check.
- `collect()` before `separate()`, `unite()`, or any `str_` verb. Those run in R. This SQLite file does not run a regular expression.
- Either pipe is fine: `|>` or `%>%`.
- Partial credit is given for code that runs. If you are stuck, go to the next step.

Each step starts from the data frame the previous step made. Step 8 prints a summary and must not drop any rows. Steps 9 and 10 continue from the data frame in step 7.
